name: William Wrigley Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: William "Beau" Wrigley Jr. is an heir to the Wrigley's chewing gum fortune.
In 1999, he took over the business his great-grandfather started in 1891.
Wrigley Jr., who was CEO, expanded the company in 2005 by purchasing Altoids and Life Savers from Kraft Foods for $1.46 billion.
In 2008, he sold the Chicago-based firm to candy giant Mars Inc. for $23 billion in cash.
Wrigley became CEO of cannabis product-maker Parallel in 2018.
A 2021 SPAC deal to take Parallel public fell through and Wrigley stepped down as CEO. The company is now embroiled in lawsuits waged by investors.
forbes_facts: Wrigley's great grandfather originally sold baking soda. He switched businesses after realizing that the chewing gum he gave away was much more popular.
His grandfather P.K. Wrigley owned the Chicago Cubs, but the family had to sell the baseball team in 1981 in order to pay the estate taxes after his death.

name: Segolene Gallienne
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Segolene Gallienne is the daughter of the late Albert Frere, the billionaire industrialist who died in 2018 at age 92.
Albert Frere, who was the richest person in Belgium, turned his family's scrap-metal business into a media, utilities and oil empire
Albert Frere' s business interests included Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL bank), insurer Royale Belge, Petrofina and Tractebel before he began slowly selling off assets later in his career.
Gallienne is not involved in the management of her holding company 	but her husband Ian Gallienne is the CEO of key participation GBL.
forbes_facts: Galliene sits on board of the Cheval Blanc winery, which is partly owned by the family and Bernard Arnault's Christian Dior..

name: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2020-2021); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi owns a significant stake in Brazilian laboratory services firm Diagnosticos da America SA.
She and her brother, Pedro, inherited their stakes from their late father Edson de Godoy Bueno, who was Brazil's richest healthcare billionaire.
Edson died of a heart attack in 2017, and left most of his fortune to Camilla and her brother Pedro de Godoy Bueno, also a new billionaire.
Edson's first wife, Dulce Pugliese de Godoy Bueno, cofounded hospital and health insurance firm Amil and is also a billionaire.
Edson sold most of Amil to UnitedHealthCare of the U.S. for $4.9 billion in 2012.

name: Sathien Sathientham
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2025)
forbes_bio: Sathien Sathientham, previously known as Sathien Setthasit, is vice chairman of Carabao Group, maker of Thailand's hugely popular Carabao Dang energy drink.
Sathien founded the company in 2002 with his folk singer pal Aed Carabao and took it public in 2014.
Sathien has expanded into large scale beer brewing with a $115 million investment in a brewery.
Younger son Romtham is managing director of listed Carabao  and older son Veeratham is CEO of retail chain CJ Express.
Carabao has a subsidiary to make packaging materials and a joint venture with a Japanese partner to manufacture cans.
forbes_facts: Carabao, which has close to a fourth of the Thai energy drink market, outsells Red Bull in Thailand.
Carabao is the title sponsor of the English Football League's Carabao Cup.
Daughter Tientham is managing director at TD Tawandang, which operates more than 5,000 convenience stores under the brand name Tookdee.

name: Luana Lopes Lara
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: The world's youngest self-made woman billionaire, Luana Lopes Lara is the cofounder and COO of prediction market platform Kalshi.

Kalshi allows users to bet on everything from sports game results to political elections to entertainment awards and more. It reached a $11 billion valuation in December 2025 following a $1 billion funding round.

Kalshi received federal approval in 2020 to operate in the U.S., and made history in 2024 after receiving federal approval to allow users to bet on the presidential election, marking the first legal election contracts in the U.S. in over a century.
Lopes Lara performed as a professional ballerina for nine months after graduating high school at Salzburger Landestheater in Austria for a season of "Swan Lake."

An MIT graduate and previous quantitative trader at Citadel Securities, Lopes Lara secured funding from angel investors including Charles Schwab and Henry Kravis, as well as firms Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, CapitalG and Paradigm.
Lopes Lara owns an estimated 12% stake in Kalshi.

name: Thomas Kwok
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2015)
forbes_bio: Thomas Kwok is the second-oldest son of Kwok Tak-seng, cofounder of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
He was cochairman from 2011 until 2014, when he was sentenced to five years in prison for bribery. He was released in 2019.
In Thomas's absence his son Adam has served as an executive director for the company.
Kwok and his two brothers, Raymond and Walter (d. 2018) inherited the publicly traded company after the death of their father in 1990.
He was appointed senior director of Sun Hung Kai Real Estate Agency, a subsidiary of Sun Hung Kai Properties, in 2020.
forbes_facts: Both he and younger brother Raymond are devout Christians. They built an evangelical theme park, Noah's Ark, on Ma Wan Island in Hong Kong.

name: Leslie Alexander
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Leslie Alexander sold the NBA's Houston Rockets to billionaire Tilman Fertitta for $2.2 billion in 2017.
Alexander paid $85 million for the Rockets in 1993, just before Hakeem Olajuwon led the team to NBA titles the next two seasons.
Alexander first made Forbes? billionaires list in 2006, thanks to his stake in student loans securitizer First Marblehead, though the Rockets proved to be a better investment.
He started building his fortune by trading bonds after dropping out of Brooklyn Law School.
forbes_facts: Alexander dropped out of Brooklyn Law School at age 21 after his father died and headed to Wall Street to help provide for his mother.
Outside of business, Alexander is an animal lover; he has funded a horse sanctuary in Middleburg,Virginia named after his mother, Evelyn.

name: Katharina Otto-Bernstein
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Writer and filmmaker Katharina Otto-Bernstein is the daughter of late Werner Otto, who turned his mail-order business in Hamburg into a global empire.
She inherited a minority stake in Otto Group and its more than 40 companies in retail (Crate and Barrel), real estate and financial services.
She's also a shareholder of ECE, the family's commercial real estate company focused on shopping centers. Her brother Alexander is CEO.
She, her mother Maren and brother Alexander share a 15% stake in Paramount Group, which owns and manages office properties in the U.S.
forbes_facts: Katharina is a member of the board of directors of the Metropolitan Opera as well as the International Council of the Guggenheim Museum.
She produced a 2016 documentary on controversial photographer Robert Mapplethorpe.
